additionalWords.meaning: n. 导览员；指南；v. 引导；指导
additionalWords.example: The museum guide answered our questions about the box.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 博物馆导览员回答了我们关于木箱的问题。

additionalWords.meaning: n. 陈列；展示；v. 展示；陈列
additionalWords.example: Several traditional tools are on display near the door.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 门边陈列着几件传统工具。

additionalWords.meaning: n. 手艺；工艺；v. 精心制作
additionalWords.example: Making wooden toys is a traditional craft in this town.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 制作木制玩具是这座小镇的一门传统手艺。

additionalWords.example: Young workers are learning traditional skills from experienced teachers.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 年轻工人正在向经验丰富的老师学习传统技艺。

additionalWords.meaning: 有价值的；宝贵的；贵重的
additionalWords.example: A simple photograph can provide valuable information about the past.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 一张普通的照片也能提供关于过去的宝贵信息。

additionalWords.example: The paper is fragile, so please do not touch it.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 这张纸很容易破损，所以请不要触摸。

additionalWords.meaning: v. 拿；搬动；处理；n. 把手
additionalWords.example: Only trained staff may handle the original objects.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 只有受过培训的工作人员才能搬动原件。

additionalWords.example: The museum offers free admission to students on Friday.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 这家博物馆周五向学生提供免费入场。

additionalWords.example: Local people work together to protect their cultural heritage.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 当地人共同努力保护他们的文化遗产。

additionalWords.example: Learning local history helps us understand the place where we live.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 学习地方历史有助于我们理解自己生活的地方。

grammar.prompt: The guide who leads our group ___ careful about uncertain details.
grammar.promptZh: 带领我们小组的导览员对不确定的细节很谨慎。
optionsZh: 非限定形式，不能单独作谓语
做；非第三人称单数助动词
grammar.explanation: who leads our group修饰单数主语The guide。careful是形容词，主句需要be动词is；leads属于定语从句，不能代替主句谓语。

grammar.prompt: These original documents must ___ away from strong light.
grammar.promptZh: 这些原始文献必须在避开强光的地方保存。
optionsZh: 保存（过去式或过去分词）
保存（现在分词或动名词）
grammar.explanation: documents与preserve之间是被动关系。must后接动词原形，因此用must be preserved；单独的preserved缺少构成被动语态的be。

grammar.prompt: The wooden box is ___, so visitors should not touch it.
grammar.promptZh: 这个木箱很易损，因此参观者不应触摸它。
grammar.explanation: is后需要说明木箱状态的表语，选形容词fragile。名词fragility表示性质本身，不适合这里；副词不能在此替代形容词。

grammar.prompt: The old photograph ___ a similar box is shown beside the display.
grammar.promptZh: 那张出现了一个相似木箱的老照片陈列在展品旁边。
optionsZh: 展示……的（关系代词后动词数不匹配）
展示……的（关系代词加单数谓语）
grammar.explanation: 主句已有is shown。空格要引导修饰photograph的定语从句，且从句主语为单数，故用that shows。不能把另一个独立谓语shows直接接在photograph后。

grammar.prompt: We do not know ___ the box originally belonged to.
grammar.promptZh: 我们不知道这个箱子原来属于谁。
grammar.explanation: belong to后需要人作宾语。who引导宾语从句，放到从句开头，to留在句末；正式表达也可用whom。whose表示“谁的”，不能在这里替代who。

grammar.prompt: In “The records that the staff examined do not identify the owner”, which is the main-clause verb phrase?
grammar.promptZh: 在“The records that the staff examined do not identify the owner”中，哪部分是主句谓语？
optionsZh: 工作人员（定语从句主语）
grammar.explanation: 括起that the staff examined后，主句为The records do not identify the owner。examined在定语从句中，不是主句谓语。否定谓语do not identify必须整体识别。

reading.title: A Label That Admitted What Was Unknown
reading.titleZh: 一张承认未知之处的展品说明
reading.level: 四级专项衔接 · 原创模拟（非真题、非新闻）
reading.topic: 博物馆展品说明、事实与推测
reading.passage:
During a visit to a local museum, Nora stopped beside a wooden box. Its label said that a farming family may have used it to keep important papers. Nora wondered why the museum did not simply name the family.

The guide explained that the box had been found in an old house. A photograph showed a similar box, but no name appeared on either object. Staff had checked records and interviewed local people. They could describe where the box was discovered, but they could not identify its original owner.

At first, Nora thought the uncertain label made the exhibition less useful. Then the guide asked her to compare two statements: the box was found in that house, and it belonged to a particular family. The first was supported by a written record; the second was only a possibility.

Nora changed her mind. An honest exhibition did not need a complete story for every object. By separating facts from guesses, the museum allowed visitors to understand both the evidence and its limits. A clear question could be as valuable as a confident answer.
reading.passageZh:
参观一家地方博物馆时，诺拉在一个木箱旁停下来。展品说明写道，一个农民家庭可能曾用它保存重要文件。诺拉想知道，为什么博物馆不直接写出这个家庭的名字。

导览员解释说，这个箱子是在一所老房子里发现的。一张照片上出现了一个相似的箱子，但这两件物品上都没有名字。工作人员查阅了记录，也采访了当地人。他们能够说明箱子在哪里被发现，却无法确认它最初的主人。

起初，诺拉觉得这张带有不确定表述的说明降低了展览的价值。随后，导览员请她比较两个说法：箱子是在那所房子里发现的；箱子属于某个特定家庭。第一个说法有书面记录支持，第二个却只是一种可能性。

诺拉改变了想法。诚实的展览不需要为每件物品都编出完整故事。通过区分事实与猜测，博物馆让参观者既了解证据，也了解它的局限。一个清楚的问题，可能和一个笃定的答案同样有价值。

questions.prompt: Why did Nora question the label at first?
questions.promptZh: 诺拉起初为什么对展品说明产生疑问？
options: It gave the wrong date for the photograph.
It named too many possible owners.
It did not state exactly which family had owned the box.
It said the box had never been used.
optionsZh: 它把照片的日期写错了。
它列出了太多可能的主人。
它没有明确说明哪个家庭曾拥有这个箱子。
它说这个箱子从未被使用过。
questions.explanation: 第一段最后一句说，Nora想知道为何博物馆不直接name the family。她质疑的是主人的身份没有确定，而非日期或使用情况。

questions.prompt: Which statement was supported by a written record?
questions.promptZh: 哪个说法有书面记录支持？
options: The box was discovered in the old house.
A named farming family made the box.
The box in the photograph was certainly the same object.
The original owner left a name inside the box.
optionsZh: 箱子是在那所老房子里发现的。
一个有明确姓名的农民家庭制作了箱子。
照片中的箱子确定就是同一件物品。
最初的主人在箱内留下了名字。
questions.explanation: 第三段明确把发现地点与归属某家庭对比，并说明前者有书面记录支持。similar只表示相似，不能推出照片中必然是同一物品。

questions.prompt: What does “the second” in the third paragraph refer to?
questions.promptZh: 第三段中的“the second（第二个）”指什么？
options: The second photograph found in the house
The second interview with a local resident
The possibility that the box contained a written record
The statement that the box belonged to a particular family
optionsZh: 在房子里发现的第二张照片
对一名当地居民的第二次采访
箱子里装着书面记录的可能性
箱子属于某个特定家庭的说法
questions.explanation: two statements之后依次列出发现地点和归属家庭；the second回指后一个说法。不要把上文出现的record误当成箱内物品。

questions.prompt: What did Nora learn from the visit?
questions.promptZh: 诺拉从这次参观中学到了什么？
options: Museums should avoid showing objects with missing information.
Explaining the limits of evidence can make an exhibition more useful.
A confident answer is always better than an open question.
A photograph is enough to identify any object's owner.
optionsZh: 博物馆应避免展示信息不完整的物品。
解释证据的局限可以让展览更有价值。
笃定的答案总比开放的问题好。
一张照片足以确认任何物品的主人。
questions.explanation: 最后一段通过Nora改变想法总结主旨：诚实区分事实和猜测能帮助参观者理解证据及其边界，不需要为每件展品强行给出完整故事。

listening.title: Instructions for the Museum Visit
listening.level: 四级专项衔接 · 原创模拟通知 · 合成朗读
listening.tip: 先盲听确定集合时间、地点和活动，再记下禁止事项。特别注意nine forty-five与ten的区别，以及photographs允许但flash不允许的转折。第三遍按短段听写，随后选3段跟读。美式英语语音优先；这不是四级真题录音。
listening.passage: Good afternoon, everyone. Tomorrow's museum visit begins at ten, but meet outside the main gate at nine forty-five. Bring your student card for free admission. The guide will first introduce the local history exhibition. You may take photographs, but please turn off your flash. Do not touch the original objects, even if they look strong. Some materials are fragile. During the final activity, choose one object and write down one fact and one unanswered question about it. We will discuss your notes on the bus back to school.
listening.passageZh: 大家下午好。明天的博物馆参观十点开始，但请在九点四十五分到大门外集合。带上学生证以便免费入场。导览员将首先介绍地方历史展览。可以拍照，但请关闭闪光灯。即使原件看起来很结实，也不要触摸。有些材料很容易损坏。在最后的活动中，选择一件物品，写下关于它的一个事实和一个尚未解答的问题。我们将在返校的巴士上讨论你们的笔记。
dictation: Bring your student card for free admission.
You may take photographs, but please turn off your flash.
dictationZh: 带上学生证以便免费入场。
可以拍照，但请关闭闪光灯。

questions.prompt: When should students meet outside the main gate?
questions.promptZh: 学生们应该几点在大门外集合？
questions.explanation: 通知区分了visit begins at ten与meet ... at nine forty-five。题目问集合时间，不是参观开始时间，应选九点四十五分。

questions.prompt: What should students write during the final activity?
questions.promptZh: 学生们在最后的活动中应该写什么？
options: One fact and one unanswered question about an object
The names of every visitor in their group
A complete story about the original owner
Instructions for repairing a fragile object
optionsZh: 关于一件物品的一个事实和一个未解答的问题
小组中每位参观者的名字
关于原主人的完整故事
修复一件易损物品的步骤
questions.explanation: 结尾直接要求write down one fact and one unanswered question about it。任务强调证据和未知信息，不能自行编写主人的完整故事。

sent.text: The guide who showed us the wooden box explained that the records which the staff had examined did not identify its original owner.
sent.main: The guide explained that the records did not identify its original owner.
sent.translation: 向我们展示木箱的导览员解释说，工作人员查阅过的记录并没有确认木箱最初的主人。
sent.structure: 主句主语The guide，谓语explained，宾语为that引导的整个从句。who showed us the wooden box是修饰guide的定语从句。宾语从句的主语是the records，谓语为did not identify；which the staff had examined是修饰records的定语从句，which作examined的宾语。its original owner指木箱最初的主人。
sent.mainZh: 导览员解释说，记录没有确认它最初的主人。
sent.topic: 主句谓语、宾语从句与两层定语从句
grammar: showed属于who定语从句，不是主句谓语；主句核心是guide explained。
explained后的that引导宾语从句，不在该从句内作主语或宾语。which则作had examined的宾语。
过去完成时had examined表示查阅记录发生在解释之前；did not之后用动词原形identify，不能用identified。
sent.examTip: 先框定guide explained，再找records did not identify。把who和which引导的两段修饰分别括起来，特别保留否定词not，避免把“没有确认”读成“确认了”。

trans.source: 这家博物馆保护历史物品，让参观者能够了解当地人的生活。
trans.answer: This museum preserves historical objects so that visitors can learn about local people's lives.
trans.grammar: 主语This museum为单数，谓语preserve加-s。so that引导目的状语从句，can后接原形learn。historical修饰objects；local people's lives表示当地人的生活。
acceptedAnswers: This museum preserves historical objects so that visitors can learn about local people's lives.
The museum preserves historical objects to help visitors learn about the lives of local people.
trans.topic: 文化遗产保护与目的表达
trans.alternative: The museum preserves historical objects to help visitors learn about the lives of local people.

trans.source: 虽然我们知道这个箱子在哪里被发现，但我们仍不知道它最初属于谁。
trans.answer: Although we know where the box was found, we still do not know who it originally belonged to.
trans.grammar: although引导让步状语从句，主句通常不再加but。where the box was found与who it originally belonged to都是宾语从句，使用陈述语序。belong to不是被动语态，不能写成was belonged to。
acceptedAnswers: Although we know where the box was found, we still do not know who it originally belonged to.
We know where the box was discovered, but we still do not know who its original owner was.
trans.topic: 让步关系与宾语从句语序
trans.alternative: We know where the box was discovered, but we still do not know who its original owner was.

2026-10-07.title: 兼职培训：用具体反馈改进工作流程
2026-10-07.grammarTip: 先划掉who或that引导的定语从句，再找主句谓语；experienced和punctual作表语时需要be动词。副词修饰动作，如check carefully；yesterday等过去时间提示一般过去时。阅读时区分“工作更快”与“减少返工”，听力抓培训时间、携带物品和操作顺序。材料为原创分级模拟，不是真题或真实新闻。

words.example: Each new employee receives safety training before starting work.
words.exampleZh: 每位新员工在开始工作前都要接受安全培训。

words.meaning: 职业，尤指需要专门训练的职业
words.example: She hopes to enter the teaching profession after college.
words.exampleZh: 她希望大学毕业后从事教师职业。

words.example: The form asks applicants to state their occupation.
words.exampleZh: 表格要求申请人填写自己的职业。

words.meaning: 工资，尤指按小时、日或周计算的报酬
words.example: The store pays an hourly wage for part-time work.
words.exampleZh: 这家商店按小时支付兼职工作的工资。

words.example: A regular income helps him plan his monthly spending.
words.exampleZh: 稳定的收入有助于他规划每月开支。

words.example: She earns money by helping at a local store on weekends.
words.exampleZh: 她周末在当地一家商店帮忙挣钱。

words.example: The manager plans to hire an assistant for the busy season.
words.exampleZh: 经理计划为旺季雇用一名助理。

words.meaning: v. 培训；训练；n. 火车
words.example: An experienced worker will train the new employees.
words.exampleZh: 一名有经验的工人将培训新员工。

words.example: Practical training gives students a chance to use their skills.
words.exampleZh: 实践培训让学生有机会运用自己的技能。

words.example: An experienced worker showed me a safer way to lift the box.
words.exampleZh: 一名有经验的工人教了我一种更安全的搬箱方法。

words.example: Clear labels can improve efficiency by reducing mistakes.
words.exampleZh: 清晰的标签可以通过减少错误来提高效率。

words.example: Being punctual gives us time to prepare before the store opens.
words.exampleZh: 守时让我们有时间在商店开门前做好准备。

additionalWords.example: Workers must check the safety equipment before each task.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 工人必须在每项任务开始前检查安全设备。

additionalWords.meaning: 机械；机器的总称（不可数名词）
additionalWords.example: Only trained staff may operate this machinery.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 只有受过培训的员工才能操作这些机械。

additionalWords.example: A local factory offered summer jobs to college students.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 当地一家工厂为大学生提供了暑期工作。

additionalWords.meaning: v. 制造，尤指大规模生产；n. 制造；生产
additionalWords.example: The company manufactures furniture for schools and offices.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 这家公司为学校和办公室生产家具。

additionalWords.example: The clothing industry provides many different kinds of jobs.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 服装行业提供多种不同类型的工作。

additionalWords.meaning: n. 贸易；行业；v. 做买卖；交换
additionalWords.example: The students discussed how international trade connects different countries.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 学生们讨论了国际贸易如何把不同国家联系起来。

additionalWords.meaning: 出口；输出（此处学习动词读音）
additionalWords.example: The company exports its products to several countries.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 这家公司向多个国家出口产品。

additionalWords.meaning: 进口；输入（此处学习动词读音）
additionalWords.example: The factory imports equipment that it cannot buy locally.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 这家工厂进口在当地无法买到的设备。

additionalWords.example: Knowing a foreign language can help when working with visitors.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 掌握一门外语有助于在工作中接待访客。

additionalWords.example: An international company may have offices in several countries.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 一家跨国公司可能在多个国家设有办事处。

grammar.prompt: The employees who check the orders carefully ___ fewer mistakes.
grammar.promptZh: 认真检查订单的员工犯的错误更少。
grammar.explanation: who check the orders carefully是修饰employees的定语从句；主句仍需要谓语。主语employees是复数，一般现在时用make；making不能独立充当谓语。

grammar.prompt: The worker who leads our training ___ very experienced.
grammar.promptZh: 负责我们培训的那名工人很有经验。
grammar.explanation: experienced在此是形容词，需要be动词。主语The worker是单数，选is。leads属于who引导的定语从句，不能替代主句谓语。

grammar.prompt: Please check the labels ___ before sending the boxes.
grammar.promptZh: 寄出箱子之前，请仔细检查标签。
grammar.explanation: 空格说明check这一动作的方式，使用副词carefully。careful通常修饰名词或作表语，不能在这里直接修饰check。

grammar.prompt: Yesterday, the manager ___ two students for weekend work.
grammar.promptZh: 昨天，经理雇用了两名学生做周末兼职。
optionsZh: 雇用（一般现在时第三人称单数）
grammar.explanation: Yesterday明确表示过去时间，句子描述已发生的动作，用hired。hiring不能独立作主句谓语。

grammar.prompt: The new equipment ___ ready for the afternoon session.
grammar.promptZh: 新设备已经为下午的培训准备好了。
grammar.explanation: equipment是不可数名词，作主语时谓语通常用单数；ready是形容词，前面用is。不能把equipment写成equipments来表示多台设备。

grammar.prompt: In 'The notes that Alex wrote helped him check orders correctly', which word is the main-clause verb?
grammar.promptZh: 在“The notes that Alex wrote helped him check orders correctly”中，哪个词是主句谓语动词？
grammar.explanation: 先去掉that Alex wrote，得到The notes helped him check orders correctly。主句谓语是helped；wrote属于定语从句；check出现在help somebody do something结构中，不是另一个主句谓语。

reading.title: A Better Way to Check an Order
reading.level: 四级衔接专项 · 原创分级模拟（非真题、非新闻）
reading.topic: 兼职培训、具体反馈与工作效率
reading.passage:
When Alex started a part-time job at a small printing shop, he thought a good employee should finish every order as quickly as possible. During his first week, however, he printed several pages in the wrong size. The shop had to use extra paper and spend more time correcting the work.

His manager did not simply tell him to be more careful. She asked him to describe each step he had taken. Together, they found that he often began printing before checking the customer's written request. An experienced worker then showed him a short checking routine: read the request, confirm the size, and print one test page.

At first, this routine made each order slightly slower. By Friday, Alex was making fewer mistakes and rarely needed to print an order again. He wrote down one problem after each shift and asked for advice on it the next day.

Alex learned that useful feedback points to an action a worker can change. Improving efficiency does not always mean moving faster; sometimes it means preventing the same mistake from happening again.
reading.passageZh:
亚历克斯开始在一家小印刷店做兼职时，认为好员工应该尽可能快地完成每份订单。然而，在第一周，他把好几页纸印成了错误的尺寸。商店不得不额外用纸，并花更多时间纠正这项工作。

经理并没有只让他更加小心。她让他描述自己采取过的每一个步骤。他们一起发现，他经常在检查客户的书面要求之前就开始打印。随后，一名有经验的工人教了他一套简短的检查流程：读要求、确认尺寸、打印一页样张。

起初，这套流程让每份订单都稍慢一些。到了星期五，亚历克斯犯的错误变少了，很少再需要重印整份订单。每次下班后，他都会记下一个问题，第二天针对这个问题请教。

亚历克斯明白了，有用的反馈会指出一个员工能够改变的具体行动。提高效率并不总是意味着动作更快；有时候，它意味着避免再次犯同样的错误。

questions.prompt: What caused some of Alex's early mistakes?
questions.promptZh: 亚历克斯早期的一些错误是什么原因造成的？
options: He received no written requests from customers.
He started printing before checking the written request.
He used a different shop's checking routine.
He refused to print a test page after training.
optionsZh: 客户没有提供书面要求。
他尚未检查书面要求就开始打印。
他使用了另一家店的检查流程。
培训之后他拒绝打印样张。
questions.explanation: 第二段明确指出he often began printing before checking the customer's written request。问题不是缺少书面要求，而是没有先检查；D与之后采用流程的行为不符。

questions.prompt: How did the manager make her feedback useful?
questions.promptZh: 经理怎样让自己的反馈更有用？
options: She asked Alex to work twice as fast.
She removed all checks from the process.
She blamed the customers for unclear orders.
She helped Alex find a specific step to change.
optionsZh: 她让亚历克斯以两倍速度工作。
她取消了流程中的所有检查。
她责怪客户的订单不清楚。
她帮助亚历克斯找到一个需要改变的具体步骤。
questions.explanation: 经理让他逐步描述过程，并定位到打印前未检查要求这一问题。反馈具体指向可以改变的步骤，而非笼统催促或责怪他人。

questions.prompt: What happened after Alex adopted the checking routine?
questions.promptZh: 亚历克斯采用检查流程后发生了什么？
options: He made fewer mistakes and needed less repeated printing.
He immediately completed every order faster.
He no longer needed to read customers' requests.
He stopped asking other workers for advice.
optionsZh: 他的错误减少了，需要重印的情况也减少了。
他立刻更快地完成了每一份订单。
他不再需要阅读客户的要求。
他不再向其他工人请教。
questions.explanation: 第三段说明起初略慢，但到周五错误和重印都减少。B中的immediately与At first...slightly slower冲突；C、D均不符合原文。

questions.prompt: What is the main lesson of the passage?
questions.promptZh: 这篇文章主要说明了什么？
options: A part-time worker should never question a routine.
Speed is the only useful measure of work quality.
Specific feedback can improve efficiency by reducing repeated mistakes.
Experienced workers do not need to check their orders.
optionsZh: 兼职员工绝不应该质疑工作流程。
速度是衡量工作质量唯一有用的标准。
具体反馈可以通过减少重复错误提高效率。
有经验的工人不需要检查订单。
questions.explanation: 全文通过查明原因、改变步骤和减少重印展示具体反馈的作用，末段直接总结效率不只来自速度，也来自避免重复错误。

listening.title: A Notice for New Employees
listening.level: 四级衔接短通知 · 原创模拟 · 浏览器合成朗读
listening.tip: 第一遍抓住通知目的；第二遍区分培训开始时间和提前到达时间，记录携带物品与请假截止时间。重点听first、then和This time，辨认先示范、后结对练习的顺序。朗读优先采用可用美式英语语音，不是真题录音。
listening.passage: Hello, everyone. Tomorrow's training for new employees will start at nine in Room Three. Please arrive ten minutes early, but do not begin using the equipment alone. An experienced worker will first show you how to check each order. Then you will practice in pairs and receive feedback on one completed task. Last week's group tried to work quickly and missed several labels. This time, accuracy comes before speed. Bring a notebook, not your own tools. If you cannot attend, call the office before five today so we can arrange another session.
listening.passageZh: 大家好。明天的新员工培训将在九点于三号房间开始。请提前十分钟到达，但不要独自开始使用设备。一名有经验的工人会先示范如何检查每一份订单。随后，你们将结对练习，并就一项完成的任务获得反馈。上周那组人力求工作迅速，却漏看了几个标签。这一次，准确性比速度更重要。请带笔记本，不要带自己的工具。如果无法参加，请在今天五点前给办公室打电话，以便我们安排另一场培训。
dictation: This time, accuracy comes before speed.
Bring a notebook, not your own tools.
dictationZh: 这一次，准确性比速度更重要。
请带笔记本，不要带自己的工具。

questions.prompt: What should employees do before the training begins at nine?
questions.promptZh: 员工在九点培训开始前应该做什么？
options: Call the office at five tomorrow.
Bring their own tools to the room.
optionsZh: 明天五点给办公室打电话。
把自己的工具带到房间。
questions.explanation: 通知明确要求arrive ten minutes early，因此应八点五十分到达。不能把开始时间九点当成到达时间；工具和独自操作设备都被否定。

questions.prompt: Why does the speaker emphasize accuracy before speed?
questions.promptZh: 说话者为什么强调准确性优先于速度？
options: The previous group worked quickly but missed labels.
The office no longer accepts written orders.
The training session has been moved to another day.
Experienced workers must complete all the tasks alone.
optionsZh: 上一组工作求快，却漏看了标签。
办公室不再接受书面订单。
有经验的工人必须独自完成所有任务。
questions.explanation: Last week's group tried to work quickly and missed several labels给出强调准确性的原因。其余内容未被提及或与结对练习的安排不符。

sent.text: The employee who checks each order carefully knows that training is useful only when workers apply what they have learned.
sent.main: The employee knows that training is useful only when workers apply what they have learned.
sent.translation: 这名认真检查每份订单的员工明白，只有当工人运用所学内容时，培训才有用。
sent.structure: 主句主语是The employee，谓语是knows，that引导宾语从句。who checks each order carefully是修饰employee的定语从句，不是主句。宾语从句的主语是training，系表结构是is useful；only when workers apply what they have learned表示培训有用的条件。what they have learned整体作apply的宾语，意为“他们所学的内容”。
sent.mainZh: 员工明白，只有当工人运用所学内容时，培训才有用。
sent.topic: 主句谓语、定语从句、be加形容词及what名词性从句
grammar: 先括起who checks each order carefully，便能找到The employee knows这一主干；checks不是主句谓语。
training是名词，useful是形容词，两者之间需要系动词is；不能省略be。
carefully修饰checks这一动作；what they have learned不是疑问句，而是表示“他们所学内容”的名词性从句。
sent.examTip: 先说出employee knows，再解释that后面的观点；翻译only when时要保留“只有……才……”这一限制，不要译成所有培训自动有效。

trans.source: 有经验的员工会在开始工作之前检查设备。
trans.answer: Experienced employees check the equipment before starting work.
trans.grammar: experienced是形容词，修饰employees；复数主语搭配check。equipment是不可数名词。before后可接动名词starting，也可接they start这样的完整从句。
acceptedAnswers: Experienced employees check the equipment before starting work.
Experienced employees check the equipment before they start work.
trans.topic: 形容词修饰名词、不可数名词与时间顺序
trans.alternative: Experienced employees check the equipment before they start work.

trans.source: 具体的反馈帮助我们减少错误，而不仅仅是加快速度。
trans.answer: Specific feedback helps us reduce mistakes, not just work faster.
trans.grammar: feedback是不可数名词，作主语时用helps；help somebody do something中的reduce和work用动词原形。not just保留“不仅仅”的对比含义，不能把句子简化成只追求速度。
acceptedAnswers: Specific feedback helps us reduce mistakes, not just work faster.
Specific feedback helps us make fewer mistakes rather than simply work faster.
trans.topic: feedback的主谓一致、help结构与对比表达
trans.alternative: Specific feedback helps us make fewer mistakes rather than simply work faster.

2026-10-08.title: 周测复盘：共享洗衣房的错峰试验
2026-10-08.grammarTip: 本周复盘不新增课程词，由系统安排40个复习或自选待学词。语法继续检查主句谓语、be加形容词、不可数名词和before加动名词；阅读先找事实，再判断结论是否超出证据。听力区分提前到达时间、允许迟到时间与预约时长。先独立作答，再订正，保留首次成绩。本文和题目均为原创分级模拟。

grammar.prompt: The notice that explains the booking rules ___ clear.
grammar.promptZh: 解释预约规则的那张通知很清楚。
grammar.explanation: 先括起that explains the booking rules，主句成为The notice is clear。notice为单数，clear是形容词，前面需要is；explains属于定语从句。

grammar.prompt: The equipment in the laundry room ___ checked every morning.
grammar.promptZh: 洗衣房里的设备每天早上都会被检查。
grammar.explanation: equipment是不可数名词，主语按单数处理。设备是被检查，使用一般现在时被动语态is checked；every morning表示习惯性动作。

grammar.prompt: Please remove your clothes before ___ the room.
grammar.promptZh: 离开房间之前，请取走衣物。
grammar.explanation: before在这里是介词，后接动名词leaving。若用完整从句，可另写before you leave the room。

grammar.prompt: Students should read the instructions ___ before using a machine.
grammar.promptZh: 学生在使用机器之前应该仔细阅读说明。
grammar.explanation: 这里要说明read这一动作的方式，使用副词carefully。形容词careful不能直接用在此处修饰动作。

grammar.prompt: Washing clothes is an ___ task, but I do not do it every day.
grammar.promptZh: 洗衣服是一项日常任务，但我并不是每天都洗。
grammar.explanation: 空格修饰名词task，需要形容词everyday；句末every day分开写，表示每天。日常事务不一定每天都做。

grammar.prompt: In 'The students who changed their washing time waited less', which word is the main-clause verb?
grammar.promptZh: 在“The students who changed their washing time waited less”中，哪个词是主句谓语动词？
grammar.explanation: 去掉修饰students的who changed their washing time，主句是The students waited less。因此主句谓语是waited，不是从句里的changed。

reading.title: A Quieter Time to Do the Washing
reading.titleZh: 在不那么拥挤的时段洗衣服
reading.level: 四级衔接周测 · 原创分级模拟（非真题、非新闻）
reading.topic: 共享设施、错峰安排与证据范围
reading.passage:
Students in one college hall often waited for washing machines on Sunday evenings. Some asked the college to buy more machines. Before making that decision, a student group recorded when the existing machines were used. They found long lines after dinner, but several machines stood empty in the early afternoon.

The group posted a simple chart showing the quieter hours. For one week, volunteers tried washing earlier and reported how long they waited. Their average wait fell from twenty minutes to eight. However, several students with afternoon jobs could not change their routine. One student also pointed out that the trial week was unusually dry, so fewer people might have washed heavy clothes.

The group did not claim that the chart had solved every problem. It recommended keeping the chart and collecting information for another month, including rainy weeks. If long waits continued, extra machines could still be necessary.

The trial showed that changing a routine can make better use of shared equipment. It also showed why a promising result should be checked under different conditions before it becomes the basis for an expensive decision.
reading.passageZh:
一栋大学宿舍楼里的学生经常在周日晚上排队等洗衣机。有些人要求学校增购机器。在作出这个决定之前，一个学生小组记录了现有机器的使用时段。他们发现晚饭后队伍很长，但下午较早时有几台机器闲着。

小组张贴了一张简单的图表，标明不那么拥挤的时段。在为期一周的试验里，志愿者尝试提前洗衣，并报告等待了多久。他们的平均等待时间从二十分钟降到了八分钟。然而，几名下午要工作的学生无法改变作息。一名学生还指出，试验的那一周异常干燥，因此洗厚重衣物的人可能较少。

小组没有声称图表解决了所有问题。它建议保留图表，并再收集一个月的信息，其中要包括多雨的星期。如果长时间等待的情况持续存在，增添机器可能仍然有必要。

这项试验表明，改变日常安排能够更好地利用共享设备。它也说明，一个令人鼓舞的结果，在成为昂贵决策的依据之前，为什么还应该在不同条件下接受检验。

questions.prompt: What did the student group discover before the trial?
questions.promptZh: 学生小组在试验前发现了什么？
options: All the washing machines needed repair.
Some machines were unused in the early afternoon.
Every student preferred to wash clothes after work.
optionsZh: 所有洗衣机都需要维修。
下午较早时有些机器没有被使用。
每名学生都更喜欢工作后洗衣。
questions.explanation: 第一段最后一句说several machines stood empty in the early afternoon，与B同义。长队集中在晚饭后，并不代表全天都缺机器。

questions.prompt: Why was the unusually dry weather mentioned?
questions.promptZh: 文章为什么提到异常干燥的天气？
options: To explain why the chart was damaged.
To show that students no longer needed clean clothes.
To prove that rain always causes machine faults.
To suggest another possible reason for the shorter wait.
optionsZh: 为了解释图表为什么损坏。
为了表明学生不再需要干净衣服。
为了证明下雨总会造成机器故障。
为了提出等待时间缩短的另一种可能原因。
questions.explanation: 第二段指出干燥天气可能使洗厚重衣物的人减少，因此等待缩短不一定完全由错峰图表造成。might表示可能，并非已证实的原因。

questions.prompt: What did the group recommend next?
questions.promptZh: 小组建议下一步做什么？
options: Keep the chart and collect more information in different weather.
Remove the chart because one week proved it useless.
Buy extra machines immediately without further checks.
Require every student to stop working in the afternoon.
optionsZh: 保留图表，并在不同天气下继续收集信息。
撤下图表，因为一周已证明它无用。
不再核查，立即购买更多机器。
要求每名学生停止下午的工作。
questions.explanation: 第三段建议keeping the chart并再收集一个月的信息，including rainy weeks。小组既没有立即否定图表，也没有立刻决定购买机器。

questions.prompt: Which conclusion is best supported by the passage?
questions.promptZh: 下面哪一结论最符合文章中的证据？
options: A one-week trial is enough for every important decision.
Buying more equipment is never a useful solution.
A useful early result still needs checking under different conditions.
Students with jobs are responsible for all the waiting.
optionsZh: 一周试验足以支持每项重要决策。
增购设备永远不是有用的办法。
初步结果即使有用，仍需在不同条件下检验。
所有等待都由有工作的学生造成。
questions.explanation: 末段强调promising result应先在different conditions下检验。A、B使用绝对化表述；C保留了试验有帮助但证据有限的两层意思。

listening.title: A Trial Booking System for the Laundry Room
listening.titleZh: 洗衣房预约系统试运行通知
listening.level: 四级衔接周测短通知 · 原创模拟 · 浏览器合成朗读
listening.tip: 先抓通知目的，再分别记录三十分钟预约时长、提前五分钟到达和迟到超过十分钟取消预约。遇到only when，注意它限制了无预约者使用机器的条件；合成朗读不是真题录音。
listening.passage: The laundry room in Hall Two will test a new booking system next week. Each student may reserve one machine for thirty minutes. Please arrive five minutes before your time begins. If you are more than ten minutes late, your booking will be canceled. Students without a booking may use a machine only when it is available. After washing, remove your clothes promptly and leave the door open. Report a fault to the service desk instead of trying to repair the machine yourself. We will review the system on Friday.
listening.passageZh: 二号宿舍楼的洗衣房将于下周试行一套新的预约系统。每位学生可以预约一台机器，时长三十分钟。请在预约开始时间前五分钟到达。如果迟到超过十分钟，你的预约将被取消。没有预约的学生只有在机器空闲时才可以使用。洗完后，请及时取走衣物，并让机门保持打开。遇到故障请向服务台报告，不要自行尝试修理机器。我们将在星期五评估这套系统。
dictation: Please arrive five minutes before your time begins.
We will review the system on Friday.
dictationZh: 请在预约开始时间前五分钟到达。
我们将在星期五评估这套系统。

questions.prompt: What will happen if a student is more than ten minutes late?
questions.promptZh: 如果学生迟到超过十分钟，会发生什么？
options: The machine will run for an extra thirty minutes.
The student will receive another machine immediately.
The student's booking will be canceled.
The service desk will repair the student's clothes.
optionsZh: 机器会额外运行三十分钟。
学生将立即获得另一台机器。
该学生的预约将被取消。
服务台会修补该学生的衣服。
questions.explanation: If you are more than ten minutes late, your booking will be canceled直接给出结果。三十分钟是预约使用时长，不是额外奖励时长。

questions.prompt: When may a student without a booking use a machine?
questions.promptZh: 没有预约的学生什么时候可以使用机器？
options: Only when a machine is available.
Only after the review on Friday.
Whenever another student is washing clothes.
Only five minutes before the room opens.
optionsZh: 只有在星期五评估之后。
任何另一名学生正在洗衣的时候。
只有在洗衣房开放前五分钟。
questions.explanation: 通知说Students without a booking may use a machine only when it is available。这里available表示机器空闲、可供使用；星期五是评估系统的时间。

sent.text: The students who recorded waiting times found that the new chart was useful, although it did not remove every difficulty.
sent.main: The students found that the new chart was useful, although it did not remove every difficulty.
sent.translation: 记录等待时间的学生发现，新图表是有用的，尽管它并没有消除所有困难。
sent.structure: 主句主语是The students，谓语是found，that引导宾语从句。who recorded waiting times是修饰students的定语从句；宾语从句的主语是the new chart，系表结构是was useful。although it did not remove every difficulty是让步状语从句；it指图表。not...every表示并非每一个都，不等于一个也没有。
sent.mainZh: 学生发现，新图表是有用的，尽管它并没有消除所有困难。
sent.topic: 主句谓语、宾语从句与让步关系
grammar: 先括起who recorded waiting times，找出The students found；recorded是定语从句谓语，不是主句谓语。
useful是形容词，chart和useful之间需要be动词；这里描述过去发现的情况，用was。
although引导让步从句，不与but在同一个结构中重复连接；did not remove every difficulty要译为并未消除所有困难。
sent.examTip: 先说出谁发现了什么，再解释although带来的限制；不要把有用误读成解决了一切问题。

trans.source: 在作出决定之前，我们应该在不同条件下检查结果。
trans.answer: Before making a decision, we should check the results under different conditions.
trans.grammar: before后可接making这一动名词，也可接we make a decision这一完整从句；should后用动词原形check。under different conditions表示在不同条件下。
acceptedAnswers: Before making a decision, we should check the results under different conditions.
We should check the results under different conditions before we make a decision.
trans.alternative: We should check the results under different conditions before we make a decision.

trans.source: 虽然图表很有用，但它并没有解决所有问题。
trans.answer: Although the chart was useful, it did not solve every problem.
trans.grammar: 英语中用although连接两部分时，不再重复使用but；useful前需要was。not...every是部分否定，表示并非所有问题都被解决，也可用did not solve all the problems。
acceptedAnswers: Although the chart was useful, it did not solve every problem.
Although the chart was useful, it did not solve all the problems.
The chart was useful, but it did not solve every problem.
trans.topic: 让步关系、be加形容词与部分否定
trans.alternative: The chart was useful, but it did not solve every problem.

2026-10-09.title: 校园讲座：从醒目标题追到原始证据
2026-10-09.grammarTip: 阅读先区分标题中的强结论和原始调查实际支持的范围；some不等于all，opinion不等于fact。语法继续巩固主句与定语从句的谓语、be加形容词，同时练习被动语态、whether宾语从句和百分比的主谓一致。材料是原创分级模拟，不是真题、真实研究或实时新闻。

words.example: Studying science includes asking how a claim can be tested.
words.exampleZh: 学习科学包括思考一项说法可以如何接受检验。

words.meaning: 科学的；符合科学方法的
words.example: A strong opinion is not the same as scientific evidence.
words.exampleZh: 强烈的观点不等于科学证据。

words.example: The scientist explained both the result and its limits.
words.exampleZh: 这位科学家既解释了结果，也说明了它的局限。

words.meaning: n. 实验；试验；v. 做实验；尝试
words.example: The class carried out an experiment and recorded each step.
words.exampleZh: 全班做了一项实验，并记录了每个步骤。

words.example: Students must read the instructions before entering the laboratory.
words.exampleZh: 学生必须在进入实验室前阅读说明。

words.example: The teacher showed us how to use the measuring instrument.
words.exampleZh: 老师向我们演示了如何使用这件测量仪器。

words.meaning: adj. 化学的；n. 化学品
words.example: The lesson describes a chemical change without asking students to mix substances.
words.exampleZh: 这节课描述一种化学变化，但不要求学生混合物质。

words.example: The label describes the substance inside the bottle.
words.exampleZh: 标签说明了瓶子里的物质。

words.example: A discovery may lead to new questions as well as answers.
words.exampleZh: 一项发现可能既带来答案，也带来新的问题。

words.example: The students hope to invent a device that saves paper.
words.exampleZh: 学生们希望发明一种节省纸张的装置。

words.example: A useful invention solves a problem that people actually face.
words.exampleZh: 有用的发明解决人们实际面临的问题。

words.example: The article appeared in a scientific journal rather than an advertisement.
words.exampleZh: 这篇文章刊登在科学期刊上，而不是广告中。

additionalWords.example: The headline sounded certain, but the article described several limits.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 标题听起来很肯定，但文章描述了几项局限。

additionalWords.example: The editor asked the writer to check the source of the number.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 编辑要求作者核对这个数字的来源。

additionalWords.example: Read the whole article before sharing its headline.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 转发标题之前，先读完整篇文章。

additionalWords.example: Members of the audience wrote down questions during the lecture.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 听众在讲座期间记下了问题。

additionalWords.meaning: n. 声称；主张；v. 声称；要求
additionalWords.example: We should check the evidence behind a surprising claim.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 我们应该核查一项令人惊讶的说法背后的证据。

additionalWords.example: A reader needs to separate a fact from a personal opinion.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 读者需要把事实与个人观点区分开。

additionalWords.example: In my opinion, the headline gives readers too much confidence.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 在我看来，这个标题让读者过于确信。

additionalWords.meaning: 调查；概述（此处学习名词读音）
additionalWords.example: Only students from one class took part in the survey.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 只有一个班的学生参与了这项调查。

additionalWords.meaning: 统计数字；统计数据中的一个数值
additionalWords.example: Before quoting a statistic, find out how it was collected.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 引用一个统计数字之前，先了解它是如何收集到的。

additionalWords.example: A small percentage of the audience asked questions after the talk.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 讲座结束后，一小部分听众提出了问题。

grammar.prompt: The scientist who explains the results ___ questions from the audience.
grammar.promptZh: 解释结果的那位科学家会回答听众的问题。
grammar.explanation: who explains the results是修饰scientist的定语从句。主句主语The scientist是单数，主句谓语用answers；explains不能替代主句谓语。

grammar.prompt: The claims in this article ___ difficult to check.
grammar.promptZh: 这篇文章中的这些说法很难核查。
optionsZh: 做；助动词第三人称单数
grammar.explanation: difficult是形容词，前面需要be动词；主语是复数claims，所以用are。in this article是介词短语，不决定谓语单复数。

grammar.prompt: The results ___ in the school journal last week.
grammar.promptZh: 这些结果上周发表在校刊上。
optionsZh: 被发表了（一般过去时被动语态）
grammar.explanation: results是被发表的对象，因此需要被动语态；last week提示一般过去时。复数主语搭配were published。

grammar.prompt: The editor asked ___ the number came from a survey or an experiment.
grammar.promptZh: 编辑问这个数字来自调查还是实验。
grammar.explanation: whether引导宾语从句，并与or共同表达“是……还是……”。because和although表达原因、让步，不能在这里引出所问内容；which后不能直接接这一完整陈述结构。

grammar.prompt: Twenty percent of the students in this survey ___ first-year students.
grammar.promptZh: 这项调查中百分之二十的学生是一年级学生。
grammar.explanation: 百分比短语的谓语要结合of后的名词判断；这里students是复数，所以用are。不要只因为percent前面是一个数字就机械地用单数。

grammar.prompt: In 'The article that Mia read changed her opinion', which word is the main-clause verb?
grammar.promptZh: 在“The article that Mia read changed her opinion”中，哪个词是主句谓语动词？
grammar.explanation: 括起that Mia read后，句子是The article changed her opinion。主语article，谓语changed，宾语her opinion。read属于定语从句。

reading.title: What a Headline Leaves Out
reading.titleZh: 标题没有告诉你的部分
reading.level: 四级衔接专项 · 原创分级模拟（非真题、非真实研究）
reading.topic: 调查范围、来源核查与标题中的过度概括
reading.passage:
At a campus lecture, Mia saw a headline on the screen: Bright Rooms Make Every Student Learn Better. It seemed to offer a simple answer to a familiar problem. The speaker then showed the short article behind it and asked the audience to find the source of its claim.

The original survey involved twenty students from one evening class. They had been asked which of two rooms they preferred. Most chose the brighter room, but nobody had measured how much they learned. The headline had changed a report about preference into a claim about learning. It had also turned a small group into every student.

Mia first thought this meant surveys were useless. The speaker disagreed. The survey could still tell the college something about those students' opinions. The problem was not that the answers had no value, but that the headline promised more than the evidence supported.

Before leaving, Mia wrote three questions in her notebook: Who took part? What was actually measured? Does the conclusion match the result? She decided to use these questions before sharing another surprising headline with her friends.
reading.passageZh:
在一场校园讲座上，米娅看见屏幕上有个标题：“明亮的房间让每个学生学得更好。”它似乎为一个熟悉的问题提供了简单答案。随后，演讲者展示了标题背后的短文，请听众找到这一说法的来源。

原始调查涉及一个晚课班里的二十名学生。他们被问到两间教室中更喜欢哪一间。大多数人选择了较明亮的教室，但没有人测量他们学会了多少东西。标题把一份关于偏好的报告变成了关于学习效果的说法，也把一小群人变成了每个学生。

米娅起初以为这意味着调查毫无用处。演讲者并不同意。调查仍然能让学校了解这些学生的一些看法。问题不在于答案没有价值，而在于标题作出的承诺超出了证据所支持的范围。

离开前，米娅在笔记本上写了三个问题：谁参与了调查？实际测量了什么？结论与结果是否相符？她决定，下次向朋友转发令人惊讶的标题前，先用这些问题检查一下。

questions.prompt: What did the original survey actually ask students about?
questions.promptZh: 原始调查实际上询问了学生什么？
options: How much they learned in each room.
Which of two rooms they preferred.
How often they shared science articles.
Whether all students needed evening classes.
optionsZh: 他们在每间教室学会了多少内容。
两间教室中他们更喜欢哪一间。
他们多常转发科学文章。
是否所有学生都需要上晚课。
questions.explanation: 第二段说学生被问到which of two rooms they preferred；文章同时明确说没有人测量他们学会了多少，因此不能选A。

questions.prompt: What was one problem with the headline?
questions.promptZh: 这个标题存在什么问题？
options: It described the rooms without mentioning their size.
It admitted that the survey had no participants.
It said students disliked both rooms equally.
It made a claim about all students from a small group's preferences.
optionsZh: 它描述教室时没有提到大小。
它承认调查没有参与者。
它说学生同样不喜欢两间教室。
它根据一小群人的偏好对所有学生作出了断言。
questions.explanation: 第二段指出标题把preference变成learning，并把a small group变成every student。D同时抓住了范围扩大和结论过强的问题。

questions.prompt: How did the speaker view the survey itself?
questions.promptZh: 演讲者如何看待调查本身？
options: It had limited value for understanding those students' opinions.
It proved that every bright room improved learning.
It was useless because surveys can never provide information.
It should be treated as a controlled experiment.
optionsZh: 它对于了解这些学生的观点具有一定但有限的价值。
它证明每一间明亮的教室都能改善学习。
它毫无用处，因为调查永远不能提供信息。
它应该被视为受控实验。
questions.explanation: 第三段说调查仍能让学校了解those students' opinions；价值有明确范围，不能推广成所有人的学习效果。limited在此指范围有限，不是完全无用。

questions.prompt: What is Mia likely to do after the lecture?
questions.promptZh: 讲座结束后，米娅很可能会怎么做？
options: Share headlines without opening the articles.
Avoid reading any report that includes a survey.
Check participants, measurements, and conclusions before sharing a claim.
Assume that a popular headline must be accurate.
optionsZh: 不打开文章就转发标题。
避开所有包含调查的报告。
转发说法前检查参与者、测量内容和结论。
认为热门标题一定准确。
questions.explanation: 最后一段的三个问题对应Who took part、What was measured和Does the conclusion match；米娅明确决定转发前使用它们。

listening.title: Preparing for a Science Reporting Workshop
listening.titleZh: 科学报道工作坊的准备通知
listening.level: 四级衔接短通知 · 原创模拟 · 浏览器合成朗读
listening.tip: 盲听先判断这是准备通知，再抓地点变化、要带的材料和截止时间。重点区分six tonight与tomorrow，听出include后面要求保留标题和来源。第二遍将通知中的动词write、include、send连成行动顺序；合成朗读优先使用可用美式英语语音，不是真题录音。
listening.passage: This is a message for students attending tomorrow's science reporting workshop. The session has moved from the laboratory to the library meeting room. Please bring one short article about a scientific claim, either on paper or on your phone. You do not need to agree with the article. Instead, write down one question about its evidence. Include the headline and the name of the original source. The speaker will compare several examples before answering questions. Send your article to the organizer by six tonight, so the examples can be prepared in advance.
listening.passageZh: 这是一则发给参加明天科学报道工作坊的学生的通知。活动地点已从实验室改到图书馆会议室。请带一篇关于某项科学说法的短文，纸质版或手机版都可以。你不需要赞同文章，而是要记下一个关于其证据的问题。请附上标题和原始来源的名称。演讲者会先比较几个例子，然后回答问题。请在今晚六点前把文章发给组织者，以便提前准备示例。
dictation: You do not need to agree with the article.
Instead, write down one question about its evidence.
dictationZh: 你不需要赞同文章。
而是要记下一个关于其证据的问题。

questions.prompt: Where will the workshop take place?
questions.promptZh: 工作坊将在什么地方举行？
questions.explanation: 通知说has moved from the laboratory to the library meeting room；from之后是旧地点，to之后才是新地点。

questions.prompt: What should students do before six tonight?
questions.promptZh: 学生应在今晚六点之前做什么？
options: Send their article to the organizer.
Agree with every claim in the article.
Ask the speaker to write a new headline.
optionsZh: 赞同文章中的每项说法。
请演讲者写一个新标题。
questions.explanation: 最后一句明确要求Send your article to the organizer by six tonight。通知还说不必赞同文章，因此C相反；B、D均未要求。

sent.text: The article that Mia read showed that students who preferred the brighter room did not necessarily learn more there.
sent.main: The article showed that students who preferred the brighter room did not necessarily learn more there.
sent.translation: 米娅读的那篇文章表明，偏好较明亮教室的学生在那里未必学得更多。
sent.structure: 主句主语The article，谓语showed，that students...there整体作宾语。that Mia read是修饰article的定语从句。宾语从句中students是主语，did not necessarily learn是谓语部分；who preferred the brighter room是修饰students的定语从句。not necessarily表示“不一定、未必”，不是“一定不”。
sent.mainZh: 文章表明，偏好较明亮教室的学生在那里未必学得更多。
sent.topic: 两处定语从句、宾语从句与部分否定
grammar: 先括起that Mia read，找到The article showed；read属于定语从句。
进入showed后的宾语从句，再括起who preferred the brighter room，找到students did not necessarily learn。
did后的learn用原形；not necessarily要译成“不一定”，不能译成“必然没有学会”。
sent.examTip: 先分清两处修饰语再读观点；特别标记necessarily，避免把证据不足译成证据证明相反结论。

trans.source: 转发一篇文章之前，我们应该核查它的原始来源。
trans.answer: Before sharing an article, we should check its original source.
trans.grammar: before可接动名词sharing或完整从句we share；should后用动词原形check。article前需要冠词an，its指文章的来源。
acceptedAnswers: Before sharing an article, we should check its original source.
We should check an article's original source before sharing it.
Before we share an article, we should check its original source.
trans.topic: before结构、情态动词与来源核查
trans.alternative: Before we share an article, we should check its original source.

trans.source: 一个令人惊讶的统计数字并不一定能支持标题中的说法。
trans.answer: A surprising statistic does not necessarily support the claim in the headline.
trans.grammar: 单数主语A surprising statistic搭配does not，后面的support用原形。not necessarily对应“并不一定”，不能换成never而改变结论强度。
acceptedAnswers: A surprising statistic does not necessarily support the claim in the headline.
A surprising statistic may not support the claim made in the headline.

2026-10-10.title: 城市出行：把换乘信息与实际目的地对应起来
2026-10-10.grammarTip: 阅读先明确乘客真正要去哪里，再区分线路名称、终点站和中途停靠点，不能只凭熟悉的站名选答案。语法巩固定语从句与主句谓语、be加形容词，练习不可数名词luggage与scenery、现在完成时和时间状语从句。材料为原创分级模拟，不是真题或真实交通公告。

words.exampleZh: 我们在航班起飞前两小时到达了机场。

words.example: Contact the airline if the departure time changes.
words.exampleZh: 如果起飞时间改变，请联系航空公司。

words.example: A direct flight may cost more than a journey with a transfer.

words.example: Check the departure time on the latest notice.

words.example: Please show your ticket to a member of staff on arrival.
words.exampleZh: 抵达时请向一名工作人员出示车票。

words.example: Keep your luggage with you while waiting for the bus.
words.exampleZh: 等公共汽车时，请把行李留在身边。

words.example: She packed a small suitcase for the weekend trip.
words.exampleZh: 她为周末旅行收拾了一个小旅行箱。

words.example: Read the conditions before buying a return ticket.
words.exampleZh: 购买往返票前，请阅读使用条件。

words.example: Keep your passport in a safe place during the journey.
words.exampleZh: 旅途中请把护照放在安全的地方。

words.meaning: 海关；关税（此处学习海关义）

words.example: The new bus route connects the campus with the railway station.

words.example: We took the subway because the roads were crowded.

additionalWords.example: The train goes through a tunnel before reaching the station.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 列车在到达车站前穿过一条隧道。

additionalWords.example: The walking route crosses a bridge near the library.

additionalWords.meaning: n. 港口；港湾；v. 庇护；心怀
additionalWords.example: Visitors watched the boats entering the busy harbor.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 游客观看船只驶入繁忙的港口。

additionalWords.meaning: n. 海岸；沿海地区；v. 滑行
additionalWords.example: The road follows the coast for several kilometers.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 这条路沿海岸延伸了几公里。

additionalWords.example: We stopped to enjoy the scenery rather than hurry to the next town.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 我们停下来欣赏风景，而不是匆忙赶往下一座城镇。

additionalWords.example: A tourist asked the volunteer which bus stopped near the museum.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 一位游客询问志愿者哪路公交车在博物馆附近停靠。

additionalWords.example: Clear travel information can support local tourism.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 清楚的出行信息能够支持当地旅游业。

additionalWords.example: Students compared transport costs before choosing their accommodation.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 学生们在选择住宿地点之前比较了交通费用。

additionalWords.example: The hotel sent us directions from the railway station.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 酒店向我们发送了从火车站出发的路线说明。

additionalWords.meaning: adv. 在海外；向海外；adj. 海外的
additionalWords.example: Before traveling overseas, check which documents you need.
additionalWords.exampleZh: 出国旅行前，请确认需要哪些证件。

grammar.prompt: The bus that stops outside the hotel ___ to the railway station.
grammar.promptZh: 在酒店外停靠的那路公共汽车开往火车站。
grammar.explanation: that stops outside the hotel是修饰bus的定语从句。主句是The bus goes to the railway station；单数主语bus搭配goes，不能把从句中的stops当作主句谓语。

grammar.prompt: The directions on this map ___ clear, even for first-time visitors.
grammar.promptZh: 这张地图上的路线说明很清楚，即使初次来访的游客也能看懂。
optionsZh: 做；助动词第三人称单数
grammar.explanation: clear是形容词，需要be动词。主语是复数directions，不是介词短语里的单数map，所以用are。

grammar.prompt: My luggage ___ too heavy to carry up these stairs.
grammar.promptZh: 我的行李太重，无法搬上这些楼梯。
grammar.explanation: luggage是不可数名词，即使指多件行李，作为主语仍搭配is。需要数具体件数时可说two pieces of luggage，不说two luggages。

grammar.prompt: The airline ___ the departure time, so please check your message.
grammar.promptZh: 航空公司已经更改了起飞时间，所以请查看你的消息。
optionsZh: 已经改变（单数主语现在完成时）
已经改变（复数主语现在完成时）
grammar.explanation: 已发生的变动影响现在的出行安排，用现在完成时has changed。主语The airline是单数，因此不用have changed。

grammar.prompt: We will show our tickets when the guide ___ here.
grammar.promptZh: 导游到这里时，我们将出示车票。
grammar.explanation: when引导表示将来的时间状语从句时，通常用一般现在时代替will形式；guide是单数，所以用arrives。主句保留will show。

grammar.prompt: In 'The tourist who lost his map asked a driver for help', which word is the main-clause verb?
grammar.promptZh: 在“The tourist who lost his map asked a driver for help”中，哪个词是主句谓语动词？
grammar.explanation: 括起who lost his map后，主句是The tourist asked a driver for help。主语tourist、谓语asked；lost只属于修饰tourist的定语从句。

reading.title: A Familiar Name Is Not Enough
reading.level: 四级衔接专项 · 原创分级模拟
reading.topic: 公交改线、真实目的地与信息核对
reading.passage:
When a city changed two bus routes, a university volunteer named Ben helped visitors at a temporary information desk. Many passengers asked for the bus to Central Station. Ben first answered with a route number, but several people returned looking confused.

He soon learned that Central Station was not always their final destination. One tourist wanted a hotel near its north entrance. A student planned to catch a train at the south entrance. The two entrances were separated by a long tunnel, and the new buses stopped on different sides. Giving everyone the same answer could add an unnecessary walk, especially for someone carrying heavy luggage.

Ben changed his first question. Instead of asking which station people wanted, he asked what they needed to do there. He then showed them the correct side on a simple map and explained where to get off.

The new conversation took slightly longer, but fewer passengers returned. Ben did not memorize a separate answer for every possible trip. He learned to check the purpose behind a familiar place name. Accurate travel advice, he realized, begins with understanding the journey rather than recognizing one word.
reading.passageZh:
一座城市调整了两条公交线路后，一位名叫本的大学志愿者在临时咨询台帮助游客。许多乘客询问去中央车站的公共汽车。本起初直接告诉他们线路号码，但几个人困惑地返回了咨询台。

他很快发现，中央车站并不总是他们最终要去的地方。一名游客想去车站北入口附近的酒店，一名学生则打算在南入口乘坐火车。两个入口之间隔着一条长隧道，而调整后的公交车分别停在不同侧。给每个人相同的答案可能让他们多走不必要的路，尤其是带着沉重行李的人。

本改变了自己的第一个问题。他不再只问人们要去哪个车站，而是问他们到那里要做什么。随后，他在一张简单地图上指出正确的一侧，并说明应该在哪里下车。

新的对话稍微长了一些，但返回咨询台的乘客减少了。本没有为每种可能的行程单独背一个答案，而是学会核对熟悉地名背后的实际目的。他意识到，准确的出行建议始于理解整个行程，而不只是认出某个词。

questions.prompt: Why did some passengers return to Ben's desk?
questions.promptZh: 为什么一些乘客返回本的咨询台？
options: They wanted to become university volunteers.
The city had closed every entrance to the station.
The route number alone did not meet their different travel needs.
They had all forgotten the name of their hotel.
optionsZh: 他们想成为大学志愿者。
城市关闭了车站的所有入口。
仅提供线路号码无法满足他们不同的出行需要。
他们全都忘记了酒店名称。
questions.explanation: 前两段表明，乘客虽然都问中央车站，实际需要的入口和目的地却不同。本最初给相同线路答案，没有核实这些区别，所以C正确。

questions.prompt: What made choosing the correct side of the station important?
questions.promptZh: 为什么选择车站正确的一侧很重要？
options: The entrances were linked by a long tunnel, and the buses stopped on different sides.
Only tourists were allowed to use the north entrance.
All hotels were inside the railway station.
The student was unable to carry any luggage.
optionsZh: 两个入口由长隧道相连，而公交车停靠在不同侧。
只有游客可以使用北入口。
所有酒店都在火车站里面。
那名学生无法携带任何行李。
questions.explanation: 第二段明确给出long tunnel和different sides；选错一侧会增加步行距离。其他选项中的限制或地点均不是文章事实。

questions.prompt: What did Ben start asking passengers?
questions.promptZh: 本开始向乘客询问什么？
options: How many route numbers they had memorized.
Whether they could walk through the tunnel faster.
Why they had not bought a new suitcase.
What they needed to do at the station.
optionsZh: 他们记住了多少线路号码。
他们是否能更快地走过隧道。
他们为什么没有买新旅行箱。
questions.explanation: 第三段明确说he asked what they needed to do there。这个问题核实实际目的，而不是只重复询问站名。

questions.prompt: What is the main lesson of the passage?
questions.promptZh: 本文最主要的启示是什么？
options: Shorter conversations always provide better service.
Useful travel advice depends on understanding a passenger's actual purpose.

reading.title: A Label That Leaves Room for Questions
reading.titleZh: 为提问留出空间的展品标签
reading.level: 四级衔接专项 · 原创分级模拟
reading.topic: 艺术教育、事实与观点
reading.passage:
A small campus gallery noticed that visitors often read the labels beside paintings and then moved on without looking closely at the pictures. The labels contained dates, names, and long explanations of what each work meant. Some students said they felt there was one correct response to every painting.

The gallery tried a different approach in one room. Each new label gave a few verified facts and one open question. Beside a portrait, for example, it asked what the position of the hands might suggest. Visitors were invited to discuss their ideas, but guides reminded them to distinguish personal impressions from facts about the artist.

During the trial, visitors spent longer looking at the paintings and asked more questions. However, the gallery did not claim that shorter labels always produced better learning. Some visitors still wanted detailed background information, so the old explanations remained available in a booklet. The aim was to offer a starting point for observation, not to remove useful knowledge.
reading.passageZh:
一家小型校园美术馆发现，参观者常常读完画作旁的标签后就继续往前走，没有仔细看画。标签包含日期、姓名，以及关于每件作品含义的长篇解释。有些学生说，他们觉得每幅画都只有一种正确的回应。

美术馆在一个展室尝试了不同的方法。每张新标签提供少量经过核实的事实和一个开放问题。例如，一幅肖像画旁的问题是：画中双手的位置可能暗示什么？参观者受邀讨论自己的想法，但导览员提醒他们区分个人感受和关于艺术家的事实。

试验期间，参观者观看画作的时间更长，提出的问题也更多。不过，美术馆并没有声称更短的标签总能带来更好的学习效果。一些参观者仍想了解详细背景，因此旧版解释仍保留在一本小册子中。目的在于提供一个观察的起点，而不是删除有用的知识。

reading.title: More Than an Account Total
reading.level: 四级专项衔接 · 原创分级模拟
reading.topic: 区分总额、用途与时间条件
reading.passage:
When a student club prepared an exhibition, its account appeared to contain enough money. Several members suggested buying better lights immediately. However, the student responsible for the records asked them to examine where the money had come from.

Part of the total was a loan from another club and had to be repaid after the event. Another part was money collected for a later trip. Neither amount could simply be treated as income from the exhibition. The club also expected a room deposit to be returned, but the return had not yet been confirmed.

The group made a simple table showing the source, purpose, and expected payment date of each amount. This did not increase the money available, but it changed the discussion. Members decided to borrow lights instead of buying them.

The records were shared with everyone, including members who had no experience in finance. Clear labels helped them ask useful questions. The lesson was not that every expense should be avoided, but that a large total does not explain how much can safely be used for a particular purpose.
reading.passageZh:
一个学生社团准备展览时，账户看起来有足够的钱。几名成员建议立即购买更好的灯具。不过，负责记录的学生请大家先检查这些钱来自哪里。

总额中一部分是向另一社团借的钱，必须在活动后归还。另一部分是为之后的一次旅行收取的款项。这两笔钱都不能直接视为展览收入。社团还预计能拿回场地押金，但退款尚未确认。

小组制作了一张简单的表格，说明每笔钱的来源、用途和预计付款日期。这并没有增加可用资金，却改变了讨论。成员决定借灯具，而不是购买。

记录向所有人公开，包括没有财务经验的成员。清楚的标签帮助他们提出有用的问题。这里的道理并不是应避免每一笔支出，而是较大的总额不能说明有多少钱可以用于特定目的。

reading.title: When a Vegetable Box Is Too Large
reading.level: 四级专项衔接 · 原创分级模拟
reading.topic: 单价、实际需要与浪费
reading.passage:
A farm offered a weekly vegetable box to people living near a college. The larger box cost less per item, so many students chose it. After several weeks, however, some customers stopped ordering. The farmer first thought that the vegetables were unpopular.

Short conversations suggested a different explanation. Students who lived alone often could not use the whole box before the next delivery. Some lacked enough storage space, while others ate on campus several days a week. A lower price per item did not make unused food useful.

The farm introduced a smaller box and allowed customers to skip a week before a stated deadline. It also published the expected contents in advance, while explaining that weather could affect the final selection.

Orders for the larger box fell, but more customers continued using the service. The farm still needed to check delivery costs before deciding whether the change could last. The trial showed why comparing prices alone can miss an important question: does the amount offered match what people can actually use?
reading.passageZh:
一家农场向大学附近的居民提供每周蔬菜箱。大箱按单件计算更便宜，因此许多学生选择了它。但几周后，一些顾客停止下单。农场主起初以为这些蔬菜不受欢迎。

简短交流给出了另一种解释。独居学生往往无法在下一次配送前用完一整箱。有些人储藏空间不足，另一些人每周有几天在校园吃饭。单件价格更低，并不能让没有使用的食物变得有用。

农场推出了较小的箱子，并允许顾客在规定期限前跳过一周。它还提前公布预计内容，同时说明天气可能影响最终品种。

大箱订单减少了，但更多顾客继续使用这项服务。农场仍需检查配送成本，再决定调整能否持续。试验说明，只比较价格可能漏掉重要问题：提供的数量是否符合人们实际能使用的数量？

reading.title: Saved Here or Sent There?
reading.titleZh: 保存在这里，还是已经发送？
reading.level: 四级专项衔接 · 原创分级模拟
reading.topic: 状态提示、证据与用户理解
reading.passage:
A student team built a practice website for collecting survey answers. During a classroom test, several users lost their wireless connection. The page stored their answers on the computer and displayed a green message saying "Saved." Most users assumed that the research team had received their answers.

When the connection returned, some answers were sent successfully, but others remained on the original computers. The developers had tested whether the local saving feature worked. They had not tested what users understood from the message.

The next version used separate messages for local saving, sending, and confirmed receipt. A small explanation told users what each stage meant. The team also tested the page with people who had not helped build it. Instead of explaining the buttons first, they asked these users to describe what they thought had happened.

The change did not prevent every connection problem. It made incomplete actions easier to recognize. The project showed that a system can perform a useful technical task while still giving people a misleading impression of the result.
reading.passageZh:
一个学生团队制作了收集调查答案的练习网站。课堂测试时，几名用户失去了无线连接。页面把答案保存在电脑上，并显示绿色的“已保存”信息。多数用户以为研究团队已经收到答案。

连接恢复后，一些答案成功发出，但另一些仍留在原电脑上。开发者测试过本机保存功能是否正常，却没有测试用户如何理解提示。

下一个版本分别提示本机保存、正在发送和确认收到。简短说明解释每个阶段的含义。团队还让未参与开发的人测试页面。他们没有先解释按钮，而是请这些用户描述自己认为已经发生的事情。

改变并未阻止所有连接问题，却使未完成的操作更容易识别。项目说明，一个系统即便执行了有用的技术任务，仍可能让人对结果形成误导性的印象。

reading.title: A Conversation Needs a Listener
reading.level: 四级专项衔接 · 原创分级模拟
reading.topic: 语言练习、互动目的与方法变化
reading.passage:
At the first meeting of a campus language exchange group, each student brought a carefully written speech. The speakers read their pages clearly, but most listeners waited silently for their own turn. When the organizer asked what they had learned about one another, few could give details.

The next meeting used a different task. Each student brought a photograph and described it without a full script. Partners had to ask two questions about something they genuinely wanted to know. Speakers could use simple words or explain an idea in another way if they forgot a particular expression.

The conversations were slower and included more pauses than the prepared speeches. However, listeners could later recall specific details about their partners. Several students said they had felt nervous, but they had also noticed when another person understood them.

The organizer did not conclude that prepared speaking was useless. Reading aloud and rehearsing a speech still had a place. For this group, though, the immediate aim was to practice responding to another person, not merely to finish saying a page of correct sentences.
reading.passageZh:
校园语言交流小组第一次见面时，每位学生都带来精心写好的讲稿。发言者清楚地读出内容，但大多数听者只是默默等着轮到自己。组织者问大家对彼此有何了解时，几乎没人能说出细节。

第二次会议换了任务。每人带来一张照片，不看完整讲稿进行描述。搭档必须就自己真正想知道的内容提两个问题。忘记某个表达时，发言者可以用简单词语，或换个方式解释。

与预先准备的讲稿相比，交流更慢、停顿更多。但听者之后能回忆出搭档的具体细节。几名学生说自己曾紧张，却也注意到别人何时理解了自己。

组织者没有因此认为准备好的演讲毫无用处。朗读和排练演讲仍有价值。不过，这个小组眼下的目的是练习回应另一个人，而不只是说完一页正确句子。

reading.title: A Booking Page and a Shorter Queue
reading.titleZh: 预约页面与更短的队伍
reading.level: 四级专项衔接 · 原创分级模拟
reading.topic: 相关性、因果与服务安排
reading.passage:
A college clinic introduced an online booking page during a quiet part of the term. Two weeks later, a student report said that the new page had reduced waiting times. The conclusion was based on a shorter queue in the reception area.

However, the clinic had made another change at the same time. A second receptionist now helped visitors during the busiest hour. Fewer students were also on campus because some courses were holding activities elsewhere. These changes could have affected the queue, whether or not the booking page was useful.

The report was revised after the team spoke with clinic staff. It still described the shorter queue, but it no longer presented the website as the only explanation. The team decided to compare similar weeks and ask visitors whether they had used the page.

This did not mean that the new system had failed. It meant that one observation was not enough to show exactly why waiting times had changed. A useful improvement and a convincing explanation are not always the same thing.
reading.passageZh:
一所大学的诊所在学期中较清闲的一段时间推出了在线预约页面。两周后，一份学生报告称新页面缩短了等待时间。这个结论基于接待区的队伍变短了。

然而，诊所同时还作了另一项改变：最忙的一小时里，增加了一名接待员帮助来访者。一些课程在校外开展活动，因此校内学生也变少了。无论预约页面是否有用，这些变化都可能影响队伍长度。

团队与诊所工作人员交谈后修改了报告。报告仍描述了队伍缩短的现象，却不再把网站当作唯一解释。团队决定比较情况相近的几周，并询问来访者是否使用了该页面。

这并不意味着新系统失败了，而是说一次观察不足以准确说明等待时间为什么改变。有用的改进与有说服力的解释并不总是一回事。

reading.title: A Room Is More Than a Photograph
reading.level: 四级专项衔接 · 原创分级模拟
reading.topic: 信息比较与个人需要
reading.passage:
A college housing office noticed that students often chose rooms from photographs alone. Wide camera angles made small rooms look spacious, while photographs taken in bright sunshine hid how little daylight some rooms received in winter. The pictures were not necessarily false, but they did not answer every practical question.

The office invited students to design a better room description. Their first version listed floor area, furniture, heating, and travel time to campus. It also included a simple drawing with measurements. Students could check whether their own desks would fit, rather than guessing from a photograph.

One student wanted to give every room a single score. Others disagreed: a quiet neighborhood mattered greatly to some students, while a short journey mattered more to others. The final page kept the separate details instead. A useful description, the group concluded, should help people compare rooms according to their needs, not choose for them.
reading.passageZh:
一所大学的住房办公室发现，学生经常只凭照片选房。广角镜头让小房间显得宽敞，而在明亮阳光下拍的照片掩盖了有些房间冬季采光不足的问题。这些图片未必是假的，但并没有回答所有实际问题。

办公室邀请学生设计更好的房间介绍。第一版列出了地板面积、家具、供暖情况和到校园的通勤时间，还附有一幅标注尺寸的简图。学生可以检查自己的书桌是否放得下，而不用根据照片猜测。

一名学生想给每个房间打一个总分。其他人不同意：有些学生非常看重安静的街区，另一些人则更看重路程短。最终页面保留了各项独立的信息。小组得出结论：有用的介绍应帮助人们根据自己的需要比较房间，而不是替他们做选择。

reading.title: What Did the New Menu Change?
reading.level: 四级专项衔接 · 原创分级模拟
reading.topic: 配料信息与选择理由：观察不等于因果
reading.passage:
At a small college cafe, a new menu listed the ingredients in each sandwich. The manager hoped that clear descriptions would help customers compare meals. After a week, sales of the vegetable sandwich rose, and a student newspaper suggested that the menu had made customers more interested in nutrition.

The manager was less certain. During the same week, the cafe had reduced the sandwich's price and moved it to the front of the counter. Either change might explain the increase. The sales figures showed what people bought, but not why they bought it.

A student team therefore asked customers to explain their choices. Some mentioned the ingredients, while others mentioned the lower price or shorter line. The team reported these different reasons instead of treating all purchases as evidence of one effect. Clear labels may support a decision, but sales alone cannot show what customers understand about their food.
reading.passageZh:
在一家大学小咖啡馆里，新菜单列出了每种三明治的配料。经理希望清晰的说明能帮助顾客比较餐食。一周后，蔬菜三明治的销量上升了，一家学生报纸认为菜单使顾客更关注营养。

经理却不那么确定。同一周里，咖啡馆还降低了这种三明治的价格，并把它移到柜台前方。这两项变化中的任何一项都可能解释销量增加。销售数字显示了人们买了什么，却没有显示他们为什么买。

因此，一个学生团队询问顾客选择的理由。有些人提到了配料，另一些人则提到了更低的价格或更短的队伍。团队报告了这些不同的理由，没有把所有购买行为都当作单一效果的证据。清晰的标签可能帮助人们作决定，但仅凭销量不能说明顾客对食品了解多少。

reading.title: When Does a Clothing Swap Help?
reading.titleZh: 衣物交换何时才有帮助？
reading.level: 四级专项衔接 · 原创分级模拟
reading.topic: 衣物交换、质量标准与实际使用
reading.passage:
At a student clothing swap, volunteers recorded forty-eight exchanges in one afternoon. The organizers were pleased, but one volunteer asked a different question: how many of those garments would actually be worn? Moving an unused shirt from one cupboard to another would not necessarily reduce waste.

For the next event, the group introduced clear quality rules. Clothing had to be clean and dry, and zippers had to work. A missing button was acceptable only if it was clearly marked and a replacement was attached. These rules helped visitors judge what they could use, without suggesting that every garment should look new.

The group also stopped giving extra exchange tickets to people who brought large bags. Each person could take up to three items, so visitors had a reason to choose carefully. Volunteers reminded them that leaving with nothing was reasonable if no garment fitted their needs.

One student proposed marking every accepted item with the words "a good choice." The organizers rejected the phrase. Passing an inspection could not guarantee a good fit or regular use. The final labels therefore listed the checks and any known defect. Visitors were encouraged to try garments on before using a ticket. The organizers reported the exchange count as a measure of activity, while avoiding claims about how much waste the event had prevented.
reading.passageZh:
在一次学生衣物交换活动中，志愿者记录了一个下午四十八次交换。组织者很高兴，但一名志愿者提出了另一个问题：这些衣物中有多少会真正被穿上？把一件闲置衬衫从一个衣柜移到另一个衣柜，未必会减少浪费。

为下一次活动，小组制定了明确的质量规则。衣物必须干净、干燥，拉链必须能正常使用。缺少纽扣的衣物只有在明确标注并附上替换纽扣时才能被接受。这些规则帮助参加者判断哪些衣物适合自己使用，同时并不要求每件衣物都像新的一样。

小组也不再给带来大袋衣物的人额外的交换券。每人最多可以带走三件，因此参加者有理由认真选择。志愿者提醒大家，如果没有衣物符合需要，一件也不带走同样合理。

一名学生提议给每件被接受的衣物标上“好选择”几个字。组织者没有采用这个说法。通过检查并不能保证衣物合身或会被经常穿用。因此，最终标签列出了检查项目和已知的缺陷。参加者被鼓励在使用交换券前先试穿衣物。组织者将交换次数作为活动参与情况的一项指标公布，同时避免宣称活动减少了多少浪费。

questions.prompt: Under the new rules, when could a garment with a missing button be accepted?
questions.promptZh: 按照新规则，缺少纽扣的衣物在什么情况下可以被接受？
options: When it was placed beside a new garment.
When the missing button was clearly marked and a replacement was attached.
When its owner brought a large bag of clothing.
When the volunteers agreed to repair it during the event.
optionsZh: 放在一件新衣服旁边时。
明确标注缺少纽扣，并附有替换纽扣时。
衣物主人带来一大袋衣服时。
志愿者同意在活动期间修好它时。
questions.explanation: 第二段明确列出两个条件：clearly marked和a replacement was attached。文章没有说由志愿者在现场修补。

questions.prompt: Why did the volunteers say that leaving with nothing was reasonable?
questions.promptZh: 志愿者为什么说一件也不带走同样合理？
options: Visitors were expected to bring clothes without taking any.
The event was intended only for people who could sew.
The group wanted to keep all the best garments.
Taking an unsuitable item might simply create more unused clothing.
optionsZh: 参加者应当只带来衣物而不带走任何衣物。
活动只面向会缝纫的人。
小组想留下所有最好的衣物。
带走不合适的衣物可能只是增加闲置衣物。
questions.explanation: 第三段强调按需要选择，结合首段衣物从一个衣柜移到另一个衣柜未必减少浪费，可推断带走不需要的衣物并无实际益处。

questions.prompt: Why did the organizers reject the label "a good choice"?
questions.promptZh: 组织者为什么没有采用“好选择”这个标签？
options: Meeting the quality rules did not mean a garment would suit every visitor.
The volunteers were unable to check any of the garments.
Every accepted garment had to be completely new.
Visitors were not allowed to read labels before exchanging items.
optionsZh: 符合质量规则并不意味着衣物适合每位参加者。
志愿者无法检查任何衣物。
每件被接受的衣物都必须是全新的。
参加者不被允许在交换前查看标签。
questions.explanation: 末段指出Passing an inspection could not guarantee a good fit or regular use。检查确认的是活动规定的质量条件，不能替每个人判断是否合身、是否会经常穿。

questions.prompt: Which statement best expresses the passage's main idea?
questions.promptZh: 哪一项最能概括文章主旨？
options: A successful swap requires all garments to look new.
The total number of exchanges is enough to measure reduced waste.
Clear quality information helps people choose, but exchange counts alone do not prove less waste.
Quality checks can guarantee that every visitor finds suitable clothing.
optionsZh: 成功的交换活动要求所有衣物看起来都像新的。
仅凭交换总数就足以衡量浪费是否减少。
清楚的质量信息有助于选择，但仅凭交换次数不能证明浪费减少。
质量检查能保证每位参加者都找到合适的衣物。
questions.explanation: 文章用质量规则、缺陷标注和试穿帮助参加者选择，同时指出交换量只反映活动情况，不能直接证明衣物得到使用或浪费减少。

listening.title: Getting Ready for a Clothing Repair Class
listening.titleZh: 衣物修补课的准备与操作安排
listening.tip: 先盲听抓住课程时长和适合携带的衣物，再带文梳理先练习、再修补、检查针脚后继续的顺序。注意工具与纽扣的提供范围；选三句各做一组影子跟读，最后脱稿复述准备事项。
listening.level: 四级专项衔接 · 原创模拟 · 浏览器合成朗读
listening.passage: Here are the instructions for Saturday's clothing repair class. The session starts at ten and lasts ninety minutes. Bring one clean garment with a loose button or a small hole. Please avoid leather coats, since our tools are designed for lighter fabric. We provide needles and thread, but matching buttons may not be available. If you need a particular color, bring your own button. Everyone will practice on spare cotton before working on personal clothing. A tutor must check your first stitches before you continue. You may watch the demonstration if you prefer not to use a needle. The final fifteen minutes are reserved for questions about washing and storage. Please collect all pins before leaving your table. Your finished garment will be photographed only if you agree.
listening.passageZh: 以下是周六衣物修补课的说明。课程十点开始，持续九十分钟。请带一件有松动纽扣或小破洞的干净衣服。请不要带皮外套，因为我们的工具适用于较轻薄的布料。我们提供针和线，但未必有与你衣服相配的纽扣。如果需要特定颜色的纽扣，请自行携带。大家会先用备用棉布练习，再动手修补自己的衣物。继续缝之前，须由导师检查你最初缝的针脚。如果不想用针，你可以观看示范。最后十五分钟留给大家询问洗涤和收纳的问题。离开桌子前，请收好所有别针。只有征得你的同意，才会给你修补好的衣物拍照。
dictation: The session starts at ten and lasts ninety minutes.
A tutor must check your first stitches before you continue.
dictationZh: 课程十点开始，持续九十分钟。
继续缝之前，须由导师检查你最初缝的针脚。

questions.prompt: Why are participants asked not to bring leather coats?
questions.promptZh: 为什么参加者被要求不要带皮外套？
options: Leather coats must be washed during the class.
The tools are intended for lighter fabric.
The tutor accepts only new garments.
Leather coats have too many pockets.
optionsZh: 皮外套必须在课上洗涤。
现有工具适用于较轻薄的布料。
questions.explanation: 听力用since解释原因：our tools are designed for lighter fabric，关键是工具的适用范围。

questions.prompt: What must learners do before continuing after making their first stitches?
questions.promptZh: 缝好最初几针后，学员继续操作前必须做什么？
options: Choose another garment from the table.
Wait until the final fifteen minutes.
Have a tutor check the stitches.
questions.explanation: 原文明确说A tutor must check your first stitches before you continue，考查操作顺序；最后十五分钟用于询问洗涤和收纳问题。

sent.text: The garments that pass the quality check are suitable for exchange, but their new owners may still leave them unused.
sent.main: The garments are suitable for exchange, but their new owners may still leave them unused.
sent.mainZh: 这些衣物适合交换，但新主人仍可能把它们闲置起来。
sent.translation: 通过质量检查的衣物适合交换，但新主人仍可能把它们闲置起来。
sent.structure: but连接两个并列分句：The garments are suitable for exchange和their new owners may still leave them unused。that pass the quality check是修饰garments的定语从句；unused是宾语them的补足语。
grammar: pass属于定语从句；第一个主句的谓语是are，形容词suitable前不能省略be。
第二个分句中may后接动词原形leave；leave them unused表示让这些衣物处于未被使用的状态。
sent.examTip: 先找出are与may leave两个主句谓语，再识别that引导的修饰部分，最后理解but表达的转折。
sent.topic: 定语从句、并列分句与宾语补足语

trans.source: 通过质量检查的衣物适合交换，但交换数量并不能说明每件衣物是否被穿过。
trans.answer: The garments that pass the quality check are suitable for exchange, but the number of exchanges does not show whether every garment has been worn.
trans.alternative: The garments which pass the quality check are suitable for exchange, but the exchange count does not tell us whether each garment has been worn.
acceptedAnswers: The garments that pass the quality check are suitable for exchange, but the number of exchanges does not show whether every garment has been worn.
The garments which pass the quality check are suitable for exchange, but the exchange count does not tell us whether each garment has been worn.
trans.grammar: that/which引导定语从句；主句用are suitable。the number of exchanges按单数处理，用does not；whether引导宾语从句，has been worn为现在完成时被动。
chunks: whether every garment has been worn
trans.topic: 主句谓语、宾语从句与被动语态

trans.source: 我们提供针和线，但参加者在修补自己的衣物之前必须先用备用布料练习。
trans.answer: We provide needles and thread, but participants must practice on spare fabric before repairing their own clothing.
trans.alternative: We provide needles and thread, but participants must practice on spare fabric before they repair their own clothing.
acceptedAnswers: We provide needles and thread, but participants must practice on spare fabric before repairing their own clothing.
We provide needles and thread, but participants must practice on spare fabric before they repair their own clothing.

2026-10-20.title: 职业与招聘：用具体职责说明一份工作
2026-10-20.grammarTip: 四级专项衔接：阅读辨别招聘广告中的具体职责、必要条件和培训安排；听力梳理模拟面试的准备、轮换与反馈。练习主句和定语从句的谓语、形容词前的be、条件从句、被动语态与副词。材料为原创分级模拟。

words.example: The position requires a high school diploma and basic computer skills.
words.exampleZh: 这个职位要求有高中文凭和基本的计算机技能。

words.example: She received a certificate after completing the training course.

words.example: The manager explained how the annual bonus was calculated.

words.example: My grandfather receives a pension every month.
words.exampleZh: 我爷爷每月领取养老金。

words.exampleZh: 她带领团队完成几个成功的项目后获得了晋升。

grammar.prompt: The candidate who has two years of experience ___ ready for the interview.
grammar.promptZh: 那位有两年经验的求职者已经准备好参加面试了。
grammar.explanation: 主句是The candidate is ready。who has two years of experience是定语从句，其中has不是主句谓语；主语candidate是单数，用is。

grammar.prompt: The training instructions ___ clear and helpful.
grammar.promptZh: 这些培训说明清楚而且有帮助。
grammar.explanation: clear和helpful是形容词，需要系动词be构成谓语。主语instructions是复数，使用are，不能直接用形容词作谓语。

grammar.prompt: If a new colleague ___ help tomorrow, the supervisor will explain the task again.
grammar.promptZh: 如果新同事明天需要帮助，主管会再解释一遍这项任务。
grammar.explanation: 表示将来可能发生的情况时，if条件从句通常用一般现在时，主句用will加动词原形。a new colleague是单数，所以用needs。

grammar.prompt: Each candidate must ___ about the interview time.
grammar.promptZh: 必须通知每位求职者面试时间。
optionsZh: 通知（过去式或过去分词）
grammar.explanation: candidate是接受通知的人，需要被动语态。must后接be加过去分词informed，即must be informed。

grammar.prompt: The supervisor explained the booking system ___ to the new staff member.
grammar.promptZh: 主管向新员工清楚地解释了预约系统。
grammar.explanation: 这里修饰动词explained，说明解释得如何，因此需要副词clearly；clear是形容词，clarity和clearness是名词。

grammar.prompt: The supervisor who ___ new staff is in the meeting room.
grammar.promptZh: 负责培训新员工的那位主管在会议室里。
grammar.explanation: 主句谓语is已经完整，但who引导的定语从句也需要谓语。who指代单数supervisor，故用trains，不能因后面的staff而改用复数形式。

reading.title: What Should a Job Advertisement Tell You?
reading.titleZh: 招聘广告应该告诉你什么？
reading.level: 四级专项衔接 · 原创分级模拟
reading.topic: 招聘广告、具体职责与培训信息
reading.passage:
During a careers workshop, students examined a fictional advertisement for a library assistant. It asked for a positive, hardworking person with strong ambition. Although these qualities sounded attractive, the advertisement said little about the work. Could a candidate understand the position from those words alone?

The class rewrote the advertisement by starting with duties. The assistant would answer visitors' questions, update booking records, and prepare a short weekly report. Previous library experience was welcome but not required. A school diploma and basic computer skills were essential, while a particular training certificate was optional.

Next, students clarified how a new colleague would learn. During the first two weeks, a supervisor would demonstrate each task and review completed work. New staff would practice the booking system before serving visitors independently. Instead of promising rapid promotion, the advertisement explained that progress would be discussed at a review after six months.

Finally, the class checked every sentence against a simple question: what could an applicant do with this information? Working hours helped candidates compare the vacancy with their schedules. Clear training details helped them identify skills they could develop. General praise did neither. The teacher concluded that an effective advertisement gives people enough detail to decide whether to apply, without suggesting that everyone will have the same career.
reading.passageZh:
在一次职业指导工作坊中，学生们研究了一则虚构的图书馆助理招聘广告。广告要求应聘者积极、勤奋而且有很强的进取心。虽然这些品质听起来很有吸引力，广告却很少说明实际工作内容。仅凭这些词语，求职者能了解这个职位吗？

全班从工作职责入手改写了广告。助理需要回答来访者的问题、更新预约记录，并准备一份简短的每周报告。有图书馆工作经验会受到欢迎，但不是必要条件。学校毕业文凭和基本的计算机技能是必需的，而某种培训证书则属于可选条件。

接下来，学生们明确了新同事将如何学习。前两周，主管会演示每项任务，并检查已经完成的工作。新员工会先练习使用预约系统，再独立接待来访者。广告没有承诺快速晋升，而是说明会在六个月后的一次评估中讨论工作进展。

最后，全班用一个简单的问题检查每句话：求职者能利用这条信息做什么？工作时间可以帮助求职者判断这个空缺职位是否符合自己的时间安排。清楚的培训细节可以帮助他们了解自己能发展哪些技能。泛泛的赞美对这两点都没有帮助。老师总结说，有效的招聘广告应提供足够的细节，让人们决定是否申请，同时避免暗示每个人都会有相同的职业发展。

questions.prompt: Which item was optional in the rewritten advertisement?
questions.promptZh: 改写后的招聘广告中，哪一项属于可选条件？
options: The ability to carry out the listed duties.
questions.explanation: 第二段用essential与optional作对比：文凭和基本计算机技能是必需的，a particular training certificate则是可选条件。

questions.prompt: What would a supervisor do during the first two weeks?
questions.promptZh: 主管会在前两周做什么？
options: Ask new staff to train all other colleagues.
Choose a new career for each staff member.
Leave new staff to learn entirely by themselves.
Show how tasks are done and review completed work.
optionsZh: 要求新员工培训所有其他同事。
为每位员工选择新的职业。
让新员工完全独自学习。
演示任务的做法，并检查已完成的工作。
questions.explanation: 第三段明确说明主管会demonstrate each task and review completed work，即演示任务并检查完成情况。

questions.prompt: What does the six-month review mean in the advertisement?
questions.promptZh: 广告中六个月后的评估意味着什么？
options: There will be a discussion of progress, but promotion is not promised.
Every new staff member will become a supervisor.
Training will only begin after six months.
The job will automatically end after six months.
optionsZh: 届时会讨论工作进展，但没有承诺晋升。
每位新员工都会成为主管。
培训要等到六个月后才会开始。
这份工作会在六个月后自动结束。
questions.explanation: 第三段把promising rapid promotion与discussed at a review区分开来。广告给出评估安排，不能据此推断届时一定晋升、才开始培训或结束工作。

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of rewriting the advertisement?
questions.promptZh: 改写这则招聘广告的主要目的是什么？
options: To make every applicant expect the same career path.
To remove all requirements so that anyone can do the job.
To help applicants decide by explaining duties, requirements, and training.
To make ambition the only quality considered in recruitment.
optionsZh: 让每位求职者期待相同的职业道路。
取消所有要求，让任何人都能做这份工作。
通过说明职责、条件和培训，帮助求职者作出决定。
让进取心成为招聘时考虑的唯一品质。
questions.explanation: 文章逐步补充职责、必要与可选条件以及培训和评估安排，末段明确指出这些细节是为了让求职者决定whether to apply。

listening.title: Practicing for an Interview
listening.tip: 先盲听确认这次活动的性质，再记录准备时间、每轮时长和角色轮换。带文听时抓住反馈记录的两项内容；选三句各做一组影子跟读，最后用自己的话复述从准备到修改答案的流程。
listening.level: 四级专项衔接 · 原创模拟 · 浏览器合成朗读
listening.passage: Welcome to our practice interview workshop for students who will graduate soon. This is a learning activity, not an interview for an actual vacancy. First, read the sample job advertisement and underline two important duties. You have five minutes to prepare an example from your own experience. Then work in pairs and take turns asking and answering questions. Each practice interview lasts four minutes, and then you exchange roles. Your partner should note one clear example and one point needing detail. After both rounds, a tutor will discuss how to improve your answers. The feedback concerns your explanations, rather than your chances of getting hired. Please keep the notes and revise one answer before next week's session.
listening.passageZh: 欢迎参加我们为即将毕业的学生举办的模拟面试工作坊。这是一项学习活动，并非针对真实空缺职位的面试。首先，阅读招聘广告样例，并在两项重要职责下画线。你有五分钟时间，从自己的经历中准备一个例子。然后两人一组，轮流提问和回答。每次模拟面试持续四分钟，之后交换角色。你的搭档应记录一个清楚的例子和一处需要补充细节的地方。两轮结束后，导师会讨论如何改进你们的回答。反馈针对的是你的解释，而不是你获得工作的可能性。请保留笔记，并在下周的课程之前修改一个答案。
dictation: Each practice interview lasts four minutes, and then you exchange roles.
Your partner should note one clear example and one point needing detail.
dictationZh: 每次模拟面试持续四分钟，之后交换角色。
你的搭档应记录一个清楚的例子和一处需要补充细节的地方。

questions.prompt: What happens after each four-minute practice interview?
questions.promptZh: 每次四分钟的模拟面试结束后会发生什么？
options: The tutor offers the student a real job.
